thread:
Arman: quick sync from the console-arch follow-up: we prototyped two approaches for authorization at tile-render time: on-demand minting of scoped tokens vs a tenant-level delegation pool. want to capture tradeoffs + rollout checklist.

Leila: tl;dr: minting gives best security & revocation semantics, pool gives latency stability.

Jun: can you quantify "latency stability"? our p95 budget for viewport loads is 120ms.

Arman: prototype numbers: mint p50 1.3ms, p95 4.1ms when control plane co-located. Remote control plane added ~7-9ms p95. Pool hit avoids that entirely but needs pool warm/refresh logic.

Rosa: important: cache keys must not include per-request tokens. keep cache key = tenant|view|permset. token only used for downstream auth header.

Priya: ditto. also consider edge-case where permsets change mid-ttl. how do we avoid stale-perm reads if token outlives permset update?

Leila: options: very short token TTL (10-20s) + evented invalidation where control plane pushes a revoke event to edge to drain pools. or mint-on-every-request and rely on TTL = 1s for super strict cases.

Jun: pushing revokes is complex across regions. maybe hybrid: mint by default, fallback to pool only when minting latency > deadline. pool entries carry a revocation-list version so we can compare at use time.

Arman: hybrid makes sense. flow sketch: authenticate -> compute permset -> attempt mint (deadline 25ms) -> on success attach token -> on timeout check local pool for entry with version >= permset.version -> if present use pool token and increment fallback metric -> if absent, use conservative read-mode (denormalized projection).

Rosa: sounds good. add metric names: auth.mint.latency_ms, auth.mint.timeout_rate, auth.pool.fallback_rate, auth.pool.version_mismatch, cache.hit_rate, downstream.auth_denied_count.

Priya: add one more: auth.stale_perm_reads to catch functional regressions.

Leila: operational notes: pool requires a secure storage for tokens and rotation. prefer HSM-backed signing for minting, and pool entries should be encrypted with tenant key in KMS. revocation path must support emergency key rotate.

Jun: how do we handle background materialize jobs? they need longer-lived creds. propose: materialize_signer mints job-scoped tokens once per job with TTL 1h and stores job_id->token mapping. jobs must check token_version on start.

Arman: here's a sample frontdoor config I sketched for the team:

```
frontdoor.auth:
  permset_cache_ttl: 20s
  mint:
    enabled: true
    deadline_ms: 25
    short_ttl_s: 15
    materialize_ttl_s: 3600
  pool:
    enabled: true
    size_per_tenant: 8
    refresh_interval_s: 45
    require_version_check: true
  fallback: pool-or-conservative
```

Rosa: nice. please ensure refresh_interval < permset_cache_ttl to reduce mismatch windows.

Leila: rollout plan suggestion:
- canary frontdoor changes (2 pods) with mint metrics + fallback alarms
- enable pool in read-only mode (no use) and validate refreshes + metrics for 24h
- enable pool as fallback behind mint deadline for 1% traffic for 6h
- ramp to 10% then 50% with perf + auth_denied checks
- full rollout and schedule key-rotation drill

Priya: runbook snippets: if mint latency spikes -> failover to pool only and alert SRE. if pool version_mismatch high -> pause pool use and revert to mint-only. emergency revoke -> rotate signing key and notify all edges to flush pools.

devops-bot: deployment planned: frontdoor/auth-2026-04-02T02:00Z -> canary 2% -> metrics gating: auth.mint.timeout_rate < 0.5% and downstream.auth_denied_count stable.

Jun: one more: add a small sampling of JWT claims in RFC addendum so SDKs can validate quickly. example claims: {"sub":"user:123","iss":"redwood-control","aud":"data-service","permset_v":"v42","exp":1610000000} . include signed key id (kid) header.

Arman: noted. I'll produce an RFC addendum with the claim shape, the rollout checklist, metric dashboards, and the runbook. tagging owners: @Leila auth, @Jun control-plane perf, @Rosa cache/edge, @Priya runbook/slo. any objections?

Leila: none, go ahead.

Priya: LGTM :thumbsup:
